## TL;DR

The Work board previously treated a failed first task request like a project with no tasks. I added separate empty and failed-load guidance, an actionable create-task control, and retry recovery. I also added a first-run prompt for projects with no configured agents, repeatable fixtures, and focused test coverage. Headless Playwright WebKit exercised the auth-less app at 1280×900 and 375×812; the measured document width matched each viewport, expected guidance appeared, and no page or console errors were observed.

## Work and rationale

I traced the empty appearance to two separate paths. A successfully loaded board with no tasks rendered each status column with a dash; it gave a first-time user no useful next step. Separately, the store's initialization catch intentionally kept the application shell mounted after a request failure but discarded the error. Both conditions therefore looked much alike on the Work page.

The store now keeps `boardLoadError` independently from its loading state and task data. A successful board refresh clears the error. A failed refresh records a readable message and rethrows, preserving existing callers' error handling. During initial setup the catch records the failure while `finally` still releases the loading state. This preserves the usable shell while giving the view enough information to avoid presenting a false empty state.

Work now presents a compact first-run panel only when loading has completed, the board has no tasks, there is no load error, and no status filter is active. It points to creating the first task and opens the existing new-task flow. A failed load instead shows an alert with the request error, a practical server-running instruction, and a retry button. The two states have distinct test identifiers for stable preview captures. Their narrow-width style wraps the action beneath the text instead of compressing it into the title row.

The Agents page's existing message applied only to custom agents and did not make the first-run path to built-in choices obvious. It now detects when the project has no configured roles and presents a direct **Choose a built-in agent** action that opens the team-building tab. The `agents:empty` fixture suppresses configured rows for review without changing the underlying config; a component test checks that behavior.

## Approaches tried

I first reviewed the live board in Chrome against the auth-less dev server. The CUA bridge could not set a controlled viewport or expose browser console output, so I used the installed Playwright WebKit runner against the same worktree server for the target widths and error observations. Fixtures supplied deterministic conditional views while the live board remained populated.

The `work:empty` and `work:failedLoad` fixtures clear seeded tasks and stop loading; the former clears an earlier error while the latter supplies an offline-style message. `agents:empty` provides a no-configured-roles view without persisting a config change. Tests check these transitions and the mobile queue's initial failure and successful retry. I also routed the real `/api/board` call to fail in the browser, confirmed the friendly offline guidance, clicked **Retry**, then let the request succeed and observed tasks return at both target widths.

I ran the UI build and focused tests for the preview fixtures and API error handling. The UI build succeeded and the focused test files passed, including the new fixture cases.

## Challenges and blockers

The primary QA constraint was the CUA browser bridge, which did not expose viewport controls or console output. Switching to Playwright WebKit resolved that gap: all three fixture states were checked at 1280×900 and 375×812, and the real network failure/retry path was exercised at both widths. In each case document width equaled viewport width, the intended state was visible, and no page or console errors were observed. The QA document records these measurements and routes.

The `repoos update` command emitted a warning that it reads the main checkout's board when run inside a linked worktree. I used it only for the task's required shot declaration and will avoid further board commands. Source edits remained in this worktree.

## Key learnings

An empty list is only meaningful after a successful request. Keeping transport failure state separate from an empty result prevents the interface from giving misleading guidance. A retry should also clear the error only after a successful board response, so users can tell whether recovery worked.

This repo's screenshot fixtures are useful for stable, reviewable conditional UI even when a live project contains a large amount of task data. For a true offline state, intercepting the request is also valuable: it verifies both the error copy and that retry clears the error after a successful response. A fixture's visible error alone cannot prove the recovery path.
